title: SOURCE_TARGETS: CREATE BINDING FROM HISTORY must not consume pending tx_read_ts through ExecuteInternal

payload.green_status: same TSO-stable oracle passed under a minimal local ExecuteInternal isolation patch; temporary source edits and probe were removed after evidence capture
payload.user_symptom: After SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY AS OF TIMESTAMP, executing CREATE SESSION BINDING FROM HISTORY USING PLAN DIGEST can consume the pending stale-read state. The next user SELECT then reads the current rowset instead of the intended stale rowset.
payload.validation_scope: local execution-level RED/GREEN with real plan_digest from statement summary and a commitTS-derived timestamp control; not yet filed as confirmed product bug because SET TRANSACTION followed by a management statement is still a semantic-gray contract edge
payload.quality_gate: methodologically validated as a state-ingress hit; product escalation should first confirm whether pending tx_read_ts is reserved for the next user read/execute statement rather than any next statement

provenance.source: S23-derived state-ingress pass on ExecuteInternal current-session path

name: CREATE BINDING FROM HISTORY must preserve pending tx_read_ts for the next user read

payload.p_check: ExecuteInternal marks the statement as restricted/internal SQL but reuses the current session state directly.
payload.q_claim: Because the SQL is internal, it should not consume one-shot user state intended for the next user stale read.
payload.fault: fetchRecordFromClusterStmtSummary runs a statement-summary SELECT through ExecuteInternal while TxnReadTS is pending.

boundary.before: user sets SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY AS OF TIMESTAMP using a commitTS-derived timestamp between row 1 and row 2
boundary.fault: user executes CREATE SESSION BINDING FROM HISTORY USING PLAN DIGEST, whose planner lookup runs internal SQL on the same session
boundary.after: the following user SELECT should still read the stale rowset but instead reads the current rowset

source_anchors: docs/design/2021-09-22-stale-read.md:102 SET TRANSACTION affects the next interactive transaction or query with staleness timestamp
pkg/session/session.go:1874-1892 no TxnReadTS isolation in ExecuteInternal
pkg/sessiontxn/staleread/processor.go:233-257 comments and UseTxnReadTS cover SELECT/EXECUTE, with no InRestrictedSQL guard
payload.method_class: state-ingress: internal SQL enters the same session state machine and consumes a user one-shot read timestamp
payload.quality_note: The RED/GREEN boundary is strong, but external bug quality remains medium until product contract confirms that management/internal lookup statements should not consume SET TRANSACTION stale-read state.

name: Pending tx_read_ts survives internal current-session SQL until the next user read

payload.contract: An internal SQL lookup that is not the user's intended stale read must not consume or clear pending TxnReadTS. The next user SELECT should still read the AS OF rowset.
minimal_observation: create row 1, derive a timestamp from row 1 LastCommitTS plus a small physical-time offset, create row 2
control: SELECT AS OF captured timestamp returns only row 1 while current SELECT returns row 1 and row 2
set @@tx_read_ts through SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY AS OF TIMESTAMP semantics
run the candidate wrapper that internally executes SQL on the current session
RED if pending tx_read_ts becomes 0 or the next user SELECT returns row 1 and row 2
GREEN if the wrapper succeeds, pending tx_read_ts remains, and the next user SELECT returns exactly the AS OF control rowset

green_signature.fix_probe: save pending TxnReadTS and SnapshotInfoschema before ExecuteInternal, restore them after internal execution if a pending TxnReadTS existed

blind_to: product contracts where any next statement is allowed to consume tx_read_ts
cases where internal SQL must intentionally inherit pending stale-read state
timestamp controls that are not proven to fall between two committed versions
noise_controls: derive @stale_ts from LastCommitTS plus a small physical-time offset instead of round-tripping a raw TSO through timestamp text
require a direct AS OF SELECT control before running the wrapper
compare the actual ordered rowset, not just the pending-state flag

name: Binding-from-history statement-summary lookup consumes TxnReadTS through ExecuteInternal

trigger_condition.phase: planner builds CREATE BINDING FROM HISTORY from a plan digest
trigger_condition.state: SessionVars.TxnReadTS is non-zero from SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY AS OF TIMESTAMP
trigger_condition.fault: internal statement-summary SELECT enters staleReadProcessor and calls UseTxnReadTS

observe: pending TxnReadTS becomes 0 after CREATE BINDING FROM HISTORY on current master
next user SELECT reads current rowset instead of the AS OF rowset
a minimal ExecuteInternal save/restore of pending TxnReadTS and SnapshotInfoschema makes the same rowset oracle pass

lessons.selector_worked: The S23 state-ingress selector found a non-NT-DML wrapper by looking for current-session internal SQL after one-shot stale-read state setup.

lessons.quality_note: This is user-visible and fix-probeable, but product escalation still needs contract confirmation for SET TRANSACTION followed by management statements.

experimental_patch: in the existing defer, if pendingTxnReadTS > 0, restore SessionVars.TxnReadTS = variable.NewTxnReadTS(pendingTxnReadTS) and restore SnapshotInfoschema
